design_gotchas.title: Weak ±5 mA Output Drive and 350 kHz / 0.16 V/µs Speed vs Pin-Identical TLV9002/TLV9062/LMV358
design_gotchas.detail: OPA2333AIDR uses the standard dual SOIC-8 pinout, matching TLV9002IDR (40 mA, 1 MHz), TLV9062IDR (50 mA, 10 MHz), and LMV358IDR (40 mA, 1 MHz), but has only ±5 mA short-circuit drive, 2 kΩ open-loop output impedance, 350 kHz GBWP, and 0.16 V/µs slew rate. Strictly for low-frequency DC precision—not fast AC or low-ohm loads.

design_gotchas.title: Auto-Calibration Chopper Input Bias Pulses (±70 pA Typ) Require Balanced Low Source Impedance
design_gotchas.detail: Proprietary zero-drift auto-calibration introduces ±70 pA typ (±200 pA max) pulsed switching currents at the inputs rather than sub-pA static CMOS bias. Keep source resistances matched and moderate (<10 kΩ) or add differential RC filtering to avoid chopper current offset errors.

design_gotchas.title: 7.0 V Abs Max Supply Ceiling and Strict ±1 mA Signal Input Current Limit
design_gotchas.detail: Supply absolute maximum is 7.0 V (5.5 V operating max), so OPA2333AIDR must never be populated in 12 V/24 V LM358DR or ±15 V TL072IDR SOIC-8 footprints. Section 6.1 also caps continuous signal input current at ±1 mA, requiring series current-limiting resistors if inputs can exceed supply rails.

design_gotchas.title: Seebeck Thermal EMF and Asymmetric Solder Joints Can Mask 10 µV Offset Performance
design_gotchas.detail: Realizing true 10 µV max offset and 0.05 µV/°C max drift across both SOIC-8 channels requires symmetric copper routing, equal numbers of solder/via transitions on inverting and noninverting paths, and shielding from board thermal gradients or airflow.

typical_use_cases: Dual-channel Wheatstone bridge, strain-gauge, thermocouple, and RTD sensor conditioning
Two-op-amp micropower instrumentation amplifiers for medical wearables and electronic scales
Battery-powered 1.8 V–5.5 V precision shunt current sensing (34 µA total dual Iq, 10 µV max VOS)
Zero-crossover 16-bit to 24-bit sigma-delta ADC differential drivers needing 130 dB CMRR
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments OPA2333AIDR is a dual ultra-low-power (17 µA/ch typ), zero-drift auto-calibrated RRIO CMOS operational amplifier in an 8-pin SOIC (D) package operating from 1.8 V to 5.5 V (-40°C to +125°C). Delivering 10 µV max input offset voltage, 0.05 µV/°C max drift, 130 dB crossover-free CMRR, 0.1 µV/V DC channel separation, and 1.1 µVPP 0.1–10 Hz noise with zero 1/f flicker, it shares the standard dual SOIC-8 pinout with LMV358IDR, TLV9002IDR, and TLV9062IDR while trading speed (350 kHz GBWP, 0.16 V/µs) and drive (±5 mA) for microvolt DC accuracy.
